text:
dana: Ran onboarding suite for alcove-embed-v1 (float32 / int8 / int4 per-channel). Quick summary: float R@1 0.711 vs prod 0.705 (+0.006). int8 close (0.707), int4 shows larger variance: overall R@1 0.695 but for short-query holdout (<=5 tokens) int4 R@1 drops to 0.662. Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/alcove/2026-03-21/ci-291

theo: int4 drop on short queries is worrying. Any examples?

dana: yes. Example pair: short QA query "best codec for streaming" float sim 0.78 -> int4 0.34, changes top1. Attached top20 regressions.

rachel: tokenizer mismatch? model uses byte-level bpe v2?

dana: tokenizer v2 (byte-BPE) same as prod. No mismatch. Suspect dynamic range & small-value truncation in int4 per-channel.

bench-bot: CI run finished, metrics summary uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/alcove/ci-291/metrics.json

theo: Can we try post-quant per-vector scaling (compute scale factor from float L2 per-vector) before normalize? That sometimes fixes small-value loss.

dana: Started a quick rescale experiment on 5k short-query holdout (queue id ci-292). Will run both L2-rescale and RMS-rescale.

rachel: Also check Spearman rank correlation and pairwise top-k overlap (Jaccard) between float and int4. If order preserved but magnitudes off we can recover with scaling.

dana: Agree. initial spearman on whole holdout = 0.89, short-query subset = 0.74. After rescale we hope >0.9.

theo: Ops: staging preview?

ops-bot: Preview available at /staging/alcove-v1/quant-int4 (tag q-int4-stg). Canary off.

rachel: propose decision rule for int4: 1) global R@1 >= prod-0.005, 2) short-query R@1 >= prod-0.01, 3) Spearman(short) >= 0.9, 4) top-100 Jaccard overlap >= 0.88. If any fail, do not enable int4 canary.

dana: Running rescale sweep, will post results here. Plan B: int6 per-channel if int4 fails.

theo: thanks, ping when ci-292 finishes. :thumbsup:
